# Regional reference terrain

Mapzen Terrain Tiles. SRTM and GMTED2010 terrain data courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey. Global ETOPO1 terrain data: U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.

- Dataset: https://registry.opendata.aws/terrain-tiles/
- Source rights: https://github.com/tilezen/joerd/blob/master/docs/attribution.md
- Terrarium encoding: https://github.com/tilezen/joerd/blob/master/docs/formats.md
- Exact source URLs, SHA-256 hashes, tile response metadata and processing: [assets/provenance.json](assets/provenance.json)

Strait tiles downloaded 17 October 2026. These tiles were modified in 2017; their modification dates are not survey dates. Regional source metadata identifies SRTM, GMTED2010 and ETOPO1. They are static geographic context and do not measure current conditions.

## Transformations

The Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb regions each use a 4 × 4 mosaic of 256-pixel zoom-8 source tiles. The Gulf-to-Red Sea theatre (22.5–67.5° E, 0–41° N, downloaded 21 October 2026) uses a 4 × 4 mosaic of zoom-5 tiles, about 4.5 km per source sample at its centre, with relief exaggerated 24× instead of 4×. Terrarium values are decoded as R × 256 + G + B/256 − 32768 metres. Nonpositive elevations are displayed at sea level. A 256 × 256 mesh uses source-grid samples; 1024 × 1024 elevation/coast and derived normal textures retain source detail. Lighting normals use a 0.65-source-pixel Gaussian filter. Relief is exaggerated 4×. Colors and illumination are designed; this is not satellite imagery. The 2D fallback uses the same source elevation mosaic.

Source spacing is approximately 547 m at the Hormuz scene center and 597 m at Bab el-Mandeb. Display mesh spacing is approximately 2.2 km and 2.4 km respectively. Encoding precision does not establish elevation accuracy. Coastlines are the displayed zero-elevation boundary of this DEM, not an independently surveyed chart coastline. Source artifacts can remain; the Bab mosaic includes one isolated 6,803 m source sample, outside the focused strait, which is not a validated terrain measurement. No new elevation claims are made from source extrema.

The app fetches no remote terrain or imagery at runtime. Assets are served locally and lazy-loaded per region. The static plan remains available if WebGL or detailed assets fail. Water has no bathymetry or depth meaning. Not for navigation, clearance, flood assessment, or safety decisions.

The renderer contains no third-party JavaScript dependency. Its geographic labels are approximate static reference labels. Optional vessel and event coordinates come only from passed source records; the renderer does not derive locations from headlines.
